questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The naming system in which every organism is given a name with two components, a generic name and a specific epithet, was given by:

solution.explanation: Each scientific name has two components, the generic name and the specific epithet. This system of providing a name with two components is called binomial nomenclature. It was given by Carolus Linnaeus and is practised by biologists all over the world.
solution.why_others_wrong: Whittaker proposed the five kingdom classification; Aristotle made the earliest attempt at a scientific basis of classification (trees, shrubs, herbs); Beijerinek worked on the tobacco mosaic virus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (binomial nomenclature)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Carolus Linnaeus

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Some fungi live as symbionts. The symbiotic association of a fungus with the roots of higher plants is called:

solution.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic. Most are saprophytes and some are parasites. They can also live as symbionts: in association with algae as lichens, and with the roots of higher plants as mycorrhiza.
steps: Fungus + roots of higher plants = mycorrhiza
solution.why_others_wrong: A lichen is a fungus-alga association. Root nodules of legumes contain nitrogen-fixing bacteria. A basidiocarp is a fruiting body of basidiomycetes, not an association.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option C: mycorrhiza

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

steps: Statement I: true, plant growth by cell division is lifelong

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A group of fungi grows in soil, on logs and tree stumps, and in living plant bodies as parasites. Asexual spores are generally not found, but vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common. Sex organs are absent, and plasmogamy takes place by fusion of two somatic cells of different strains. Which pair consists only of fungi of this group?

solution.explanation: The features listed are those of basidiomycetes: they grow in soil, on logs and tree stumps and in living plant bodies as parasites (rusts and smuts); asexual spores are generally not found but fragmentation is common; sex organs are absent and plasmogamy is by fusion of somatic cells of different strains. Agaricus (mushroom), Ustilago (smut) and Puccinia (rust fungus) are examples.
steps: No asexual spores, no sex organs, somatic plasmogamy → basidiomycetes
solution.why_others_wrong: Neurospora and Claviceps are ascomycetes; Mucor and Albugo are phycomycetes; Alternaria and Trichoderma are deuteromycetes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi (Basidiomycetes)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Ustilago and Puccinia

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In Whittaker's table of the characteristics of the five kingdoms, in how many kingdoms is a cell wall present in at least some members?

solution.concept: Cell wall across the five kingdoms
solution.explanation: In Whittaker's table, the cell wall is non-cellulosic (polysaccharide + amino acid) in Monera, present in some Protista, present without cellulose in Fungi and present (cellulose) in Plantae. Only Animalia has no cell wall. So 4 kingdoms have a cell wall in at least some members.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 leaves out Protista, where only some members have a cell wall. 5 forgets that animal cells lack a cell wall. 2 counts only the kingdoms with a cellulose or chitin wall and drops Monera too.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Introduction (Table 2.1, characteristics of the five kingdoms)
solution.final_answer: Option B: 4

solution.explanation: Kingdom Protista includes chrysophytes, dinoflagellates (e.g. Gonyaulax), euglenoids, slime moulds and protozoans; Plasmodium is a sporozoan and Trypanosoma a flagellated protozoan. Mycoplasma is a wall-less bacterium (Monera), and Penicillium is an ascomycete fungus (Fungi).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: An organism is prokaryotic and autotrophic, has a non-cellulosic cell wall, and may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous; its colonies are surrounded by a gelatinous sheath, some members fix nitrogen in specialised cells, and it often forms blooms in polluted water bodies. It is:

options.text: a dinoflagellate, placed in kingdom Protista
a cyanobacterium, placed in kingdom Monera
a green alga, placed in kingdom Plantae
a chrysophyte, placed in kingdom Protista

solution.explanation: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are photosynthetic autotrophs with chlorophyll a. They are unicellular, colonial or filamentous, freshwater, marine or terrestrial; the colonies are generally surrounded by a gelatinous sheath; some, like Nostoc and Anabaena, fix atmospheric nitrogen in heterocysts; and they often form blooms in polluted water bodies. Being prokaryotes, they belong to kingdom Monera.
solution.why_others_wrong: Dinoflagellates, chrysophytes and green algae are eukaryotes; a prokaryotic cell rules all three out.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera (Eubacteria)
solution.final_answer: Option B: a cyanobacterium, placed in kingdom Monera

solution.explanation: Bacteria of extreme salty areas are halophiles, which are archaebacteria, along with thermoacidophiles (hot springs) and methanogens (marshy areas). Their differently structured cell wall helps them survive in harsh habitats. So A is false. R is true: the true bacteria or eubacteria are characterised by a rigid cell wall and, if motile, a flagellum.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera (Archaebacteria; Eubacteria)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

Nostoc is a photosynthetic cyanobacterium, and dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax are mostly marine and photosynthetic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a prion from a viroid?

options.text: A prion consists of abnormally folded protein, whereas a viroid is a free RNA that lacks a protein coat
A prion is a free RNA, whereas a viroid consists of abnormally folded protein
Both consist of a nucleic acid enclosed in a protein capsid
A prion contains DNA in a capsid, whereas a viroid contains RNA of high molecular weight

solution.explanation: A viroid, discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971, is a free RNA that lacks the protein coat found in viruses, and its RNA is of low molecular weight. Prions are infectious agents consisting of abnormally folded protein, similar in size to viruses; they cause diseases such as bovine spongiform encephalopathy in cattle.
steps: Viroid: free low molecular weight RNA, no protein coat
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option reverses the two. A capsid around nucleic acid describes a virus, not either of these. Viroid RNA is of low, not high, molecular weight.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option A: A prion consists of abnormally folded protein, whereas a viroid is a free RNA that lacks a protein coat

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In gymnosperms, the cones bearing microsporophylls with microsporangia are called:

solution.explanation: Gymnosperms are heterosporous. The microsporophylls bearing microsporangia are arranged spirally along an axis to form lax or compact cones; the cones bearing microsporophylls are called microsporangiate or male strobili. Pollen grains develop within the microsporangia.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Members of Rhodophyceae (red algae) usually reproduce vegetatively by:

solution.explanation: The red algae usually reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation. They reproduce asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile gametes; sexual reproduction is oogamous and followed by complex post-fertilisation developments.
solution.why_others_wrong: Red algae have no flagellated stages, so no zoospores. Gemmae are formed by liverworts, and budding in the secondary protonema is seen in mosses.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Rhodophyceae)
solution.final_answer: Option D: fragmentation

questions.subject: Botany

the prothallus, a small free-living gametophyte

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A seed plant bears naked ovules on megasporophylls, and its pollen grains are carried by air currents to the opening of the ovules. Which of the following statements about this plant are correct?

(a) Its seeds are not covered by a fruit.
(b) It produces haploid microspores and megaspores.
(c) Its gametophytes have an independent, free-living existence.
(d) Its main plant body is a sporophyte with true roots, stem and leaves.
(e) Its ovules are borne on the microsporophylls.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The plant described is a gymnosperm. Gymnosperms are heterosporous (haploid microspores and megaspores); the main plant body is a sporophyte with roots, stem and leaves; the ovules borne on megasporophylls are not enclosed by an ovary, so the seeds are naked. The male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence, and the microsporophylls bear microsporangia, not ovules.
steps: (c): false, gametophytes are retained on the sporophyte
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (c) or (e), or leaves out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Marchantia, the gemma cups are borne on the sporophyte.
Statement II: In mosses, the spores are formed within the capsule after meiosis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Gemmae and spore formation in bryophytes
solution.explanation: In liverworts such as Marchantia, asexual reproduction is by gemmae, which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli, i.e. on the gametophyte. The bryophyte sporophyte (foot, seta, capsule) is attached to the gametophyte; in the capsule, spores are formed after meiosis.
steps: Statement I: false, gemma cups are on the gametophyte thallus
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes (Liverworts; Mosses)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In which of the following is one generation NOT free-living, but remains attached to or retained on the other generation?

(a) The sporophyte of a moss
(b) The sporophyte of a liverwort
(c) The prothallus of a fern
(d) The female gametophyte of a gymnosperm
(e) The mature sporophyte of a fern

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In bryophytes the sporophyte is not free-living but attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte, from which it derives nourishment. In gymnosperms the gametophytes remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophyte. In pteridophytes both generations are free-living: the prothallus is a small free-living gametophyte and the main plant body is an independent sporophyte.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes a fern generation, which is free-living, or leaves out one of the dependent generations.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes; Pteridophytes; Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In gymnosperms, water is required for the antherozoids to swim to the archegonia.
Reason (R): In gymnosperms, the pollen tube carrying the male gametes grows towards the archegonia in the ovules.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Gymnosperm pollen grains are carried by air currents to the opening of the ovules. The pollen tube carrying the male gametes grows towards the archegonia and discharges the gametes near the mouth of the archegonia. So fertilisation does not depend on water for swimming antherozoids, as it does in bryophytes and pteridophytes. A is false, R is true.
steps: A: false, male gametes reach the archegonia through the pollen tube
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Each stamen, which represents the male reproductive organ of a flower, consists of:

options.text: a stalk or filament and an anther

solution.explanation: The androecium is composed of stamens. Each stamen consists of a stalk or filament and an anther. Each anther is usually bilobed and each lobe has two chambers, the pollen sacs, in which pollen grains are produced.
solution.why_others_wrong: Stigma, style and ovary are parts of a carpel; the pedicel and thalamus are the flower stalk and its swollen end.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower (Androecium)
solution.final_answer: Option B: a stalk or filament and an anther

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT lists the main functions of the root system. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

options.text: Providing a proper anchorage to the plant parts

solution.explanation: The main functions of the root system are absorption of water and minerals from the soil, providing a proper anchorage to the plant parts, storing reserve food material and synthesis of plant growth regulators. Photosynthesis is a function of leaves (and of green stems in some plants), not of the root system.
steps: Root: absorption, anchorage, food storage, synthesis of plant growth regulators
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are all listed by NCERT as functions of the root system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Root
solution.final_answer: Option C: Photosynthesis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The arrangement of ovules within the ovary is known as:

solution.explanation: The arrangement of ovules within the ovary is known as placentation; its main types are marginal, axile, parietal, basal, central and free central.
solution.why_others_wrong: Aestivation is the arrangement of sepals or petals in a bud, phyllotaxy the arrangement of leaves on the stem, and venation the arrangement of veins in the lamina.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower (Gynoecium)
solution.final_answer: Option D: placentation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The mode of arrangement of sepals or petals in a floral bud with respect to the other members of the same whorl is known as:

solution.explanation: The mode of arrangement of sepals or petals in a floral bud with respect to the other members of the same whorl is known as aestivation. Its main types are valvate, twisted, imbricate and vexillary.
steps: Arrangement of sepals or petals in bud → aestivation
solution.why_others_wrong: Placentation refers to ovules in the ovary, inflorescence to flowers on the floral axis, and phyllotaxy to leaves on the stem.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower (Aestivation)
solution.final_answer: Option A: aestivation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The fruit is a characteristic feature of the flowering plants.
Statement II: Leaves are the most important vegetative organs for photosynthesis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that the fruit is a characteristic feature of the flowering plants; it is a mature or ripened ovary developed after fertilisation. It also states that leaves are the most important vegetative organs for photosynthesis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Leaf; The Fruit
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plant) with List-II (storage organ).

List-I:
A. Sweet potato
B. Carrot
C. Zaminkand
D. Garlic

List-II:
I. Fleshy leaves
II. Swollen adventitious roots
III. Swollen tap root
IV. Underground stem

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Food is stored in swollen adventitious roots in sweet potato and in the swollen tap root in carrot. Underground stems of potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand and Colocasia store food. The fleshy leaves of onion and garlic store food.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the two kinds of storage root, or swap the stem and the leaves.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Root; The Stem; The Leaf (modifications)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the floral formula of the family Fabaceae, the androecium is written as A(9)+1. This means that the flower has:

options.text: nine stamens united with the petals and one sterile stamen (staminode)
ten stamens, nine of which are united into one bundle while one is free (diadelphous)
ten free stamens arranged in two whorls

solution.concept: Reading the androecium in a floral formula
solution.explanation: In a floral formula, fusion is shown by enclosing the figure within brackets. In Fabaceae the androecium has ten stamens and is diadelphous: nine are united into one bundle, written (9), and one is free, written +1. The anthers are dithecous.
solution.why_others_wrong: Union with petals (epipetaly) is shown by a line joining C and A, not by brackets. 'Free in two whorls' ignores the brackets. The carpel is shown separately by G1.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Fabaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option B: ten stamens, nine of which are united into one bundle while one is free (diadelphous)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mustard plants have a tap root system.
Reason (R): In mustard, the primary root formed by direct elongation of the radicle grows inside the soil and bears lateral roots of several orders.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In majority of dicotyledonous plants the direct elongation of the radicle leads to the formation of the primary root, which grows inside the soil and bears lateral roots of several orders (secondary, tertiary roots). The primary root and its branches constitute the tap root system, as seen in mustard. R describes exactly what makes it a tap root system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Root
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the leaf are correct?

(a) A typical leaf consists of three main parts: the leaf base, the petiole and the lamina.
(b) The leaf base may bear two lateral small leaf-like structures called stipules.
(c) The petiole helps hold the blade to light.
(d) In a pinnately compound leaf, the leaflets are attached at a common point, the tip of the petiole.
(e) The lamina has a prominent middle vein called the midrib.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A typical leaf has a leaf base, petiole and lamina. The leaf is attached to the stem by the leaf base, which may bear two lateral small leaf-like stipules. The petiole helps hold the blade to light. The lamina is the green expanded part with veins and veinlets, and the middle prominent vein is the midrib. In a pinnately compound leaf the leaflets lie on a common axis, the rachis; leaflets attached at the tip of the petiole make a palmately compound leaf.
steps: (d): false, this describes a palmately compound leaf
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (d) or leaves out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Leaf
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a dicotyledonous seed, the embryo consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons.
Statement II: In the embryo of maize, the coleoptile encloses the radicle.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Embryos of dicot and monocot seeds
solution.explanation: The embryo of a dicotyledonous seed consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons; the radicle and plumule are at the two ends of the axis. In the maize embryo there is one shield-shaped cotyledon, the scutellum; the plumule is enclosed in a sheath called the coleoptile and the radicle in a sheath called the coleorhiza.
steps: Statement II: false, the coleoptile encloses the plumule
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Seed
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A flower is bisexual and actinomorphic, with six tepals in two whorls, six stamens attached to the perianth, and a superior, tricarpellary, syncarpous ovary. Which of the following plants could bear this flower?

solution.explanation: The features are those of Liliaceae: perianth of six tepals (3 + 3), six epiphyllous stamens (3 + 3) and a superior, tricarpellary, syncarpous ovary. Tulip and Gloriosa are ornamental plants of Liliaceae.
steps: P(3+3), A3+3 epiphyllous, G(3) superior → Liliaceae
solution.why_others_wrong: Petunia (Solanaceae) has a pentamerous flower with bicarpellary ovary. Lupin (Fabaceae) has a zygomorphic flower with one carpel. China rose has monoadelphous stamens, a distinct calyx and corolla.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Liliaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Tulip

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a modification of the stem?

solution.explanation: Stem tendrils develop from axillary buds in gourds such as cucumber, pumpkin and watermelon. Axillary buds of stems are modified into thorns in Citrus and Bougainvillea. In Opuntia the stem is modified into flattened green structures that photosynthesise. In cacti, the leaves are modified into spines.
steps: Watermelon tendril, Bougainvillea thorn, Opuntia flattened stem → stem
solution.why_others_wrong: Tendrils of watermelon, thorns of Bougainvillea and the flattened structures of Opuntia are all modified stems.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Stem; The Leaf (modifications)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Spines of cactus

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements correctly compare the families Solanaceae and Liliaceae?

(a) Both have a bilocular ovary.
(b) Both have axile placentation.
(c) The stamens are epipetalous in Solanaceae and epiphyllous in Liliaceae.
(d) Both have endospermous seeds.
(e) Both have a persistent calyx.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Solanaceae: bicarpellary, syncarpous, bilocular ovary with axile placentation; five epipetalous stamens; calyx persistent; seeds many, endospermous. Liliaceae: tricarpellary, syncarpous, trilocular ovary with axile placentation; six tepals, six epiphyllous stamens; seeds endospermous. Liliaceae has a perianth, not a separate calyx, so it cannot have a persistent calyx.
steps: (e): false, Liliaceae has tepals, not a calyx
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (a) or (e), or leaves out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Solanaceae; Liliaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In the inflorescence of a plant, the older flowers are at the base and the younger flowers towards the apex of the main axis. Which of the following statements about it are correct?

(a) The inflorescence is racemose.
(b) The main axis has terminated in a flower.
(c) Plants of the family Fabaceae have this type of inflorescence.
(d) The inflorescence of Liliaceae, often in umbellate clusters, is of this type.
(e) The flowers are borne in acropetal succession.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In racemose inflorescences the main axis continues to grow and the flowers are borne laterally in acropetal succession, so older flowers are lower and younger flowers nearer the apex. In cymose inflorescences the main axis terminates in a flower and flowers are borne in basipetal order. Fabaceae has a racemose inflorescence; Liliaceae has a solitary or cymose inflorescence, often in umbellate clusters.
steps: Older below, younger above → acropetal → racemose
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (b) or (d), which describe cymose features, or omits a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Inflorescence; Description of Some Important Families
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The floral formula of Fabaceae is % ⚥ K(5) C1+2+(2) A(9)+1 G1. Counting every individual sepal, petal, stamen and carpel separately, how many floral members does one such flower have?

solution.concept: Counting floral members from a formula
solution.explanation: Brackets show fusion, not a single member. K(5) = 5 united sepals; C1+2+(2) = 1 standard + 2 wings + 2 united keel petals = 5; A(9)+1 = 10 stamens; G1 = 1 carpel. Total = 5 + 5 + 10 + 1 = 21.
solution.why_others_wrong: 17 counts the five fused sepals as one member. 13 counts the stamens as two units (one bundle + one free). 20 counts the two fused keel petals as a single petal.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Fabaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option D: 21

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: On the basis of its floral formula, a flower of Liliaceae is trimerous.
Statement II: On the basis of its floral formula, a flower of Solanaceae is tetramerous.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A flower is trimerous, tetramerous or pentamerous when its floral appendages are in multiples of 3, 4 or 5. Liliaceae: P(3+3) A3+3 G(3), all in threes, so trimerous. Solanaceae: K(5) C(5) A5 G(2), the perianth whorls and stamens in fives, so pentamerous, not tetramerous.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower; Description of Some Important Families
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In epigynous flowers, the ovary is superior.
Reason (R): In hypogynous flowers, the gynoecium occupies the highest position and the other parts are situated below it.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In hypogynous flowers the gynoecium occupies the highest position and the other parts lie below it; the ovary is superior (mustard, china rose, brinjal). In epigynous flowers the margin of the thalamus grows upward, encloses the ovary completely and fuses with it, and the other parts arise above the ovary, so the ovary is inferior (guava, cucumber, ray florets of sunflower). A is false, R is true.
steps: A: false, an epigynous flower has an inferior ovary
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower (position of floral parts on the thalamus)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Growth in plants is largely restricted to specialised regions of active cell division. These regions are called:

solution.explanation: Growth in plants is largely restricted to specialised regions of active cell division called meristems (Gk. meristos: divided). Plants have apical, intercalary and lateral meristems.
steps: Regions of active cell division → meristems
solution.why_others_wrong: Permanent tissues are cells that have lost the ability to divide. Complex tissues (xylem, phloem) are made of more than one cell type. The stele is all the tissue inside the endodermis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Meristematic Tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option A: meristems

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: On the basis of their structure and location, the tissues of a plant are grouped into three tissue systems. These are the:

options.text: meristematic, permanent and secretory tissue systems
simple, complex and secretory tissue systems
epidermal, ground (fundamental) and vascular (conducting) tissue systems
apical, intercalary and lateral tissue systems

solution.explanation: The structure of tissues varies with their location in the plant body. On this basis there are three tissue systems: the epidermal tissue system, the ground or fundamental tissue system and the vascular or conducting tissue system.
solution.why_others_wrong: Meristematic and permanent, and simple and complex, are kinds of tissues, not tissue systems. Apical, intercalary and lateral are kinds of meristems.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System
solution.final_answer: Option C: epidermal, ground (fundamental) and vascular (conducting) tissue systems

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs consists only of simple permanent tissues?

solution.explanation: A simple tissue is made of only one type of cell; the simple permanent tissues are parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma. Complex tissues are made of more than one type of cell working together as a unit; xylem and phloem are complex tissues.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong pair contains xylem or phloem, which are complex tissues.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Permanent Tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Collenchyma and sclerenchyma

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The epidermal tissue system forms the outermost covering of the whole plant body.
Statement II: The vascular system consists of complex tissues, the phloem and the xylem.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The epidermal tissue system forms the outer-most covering of the whole plant body and comprises epidermal cells, stomata and the epidermal appendages (trichomes and hairs). The vascular system consists of the complex tissues phloem and xylem, which together form the vascular bundles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
How many of the following are dead at maturity, according to NCERT?
Tracheids, vessel members, sclereids, phloem fibres, xylem parenchyma, companion cells, sieve tube elements, collenchyma cells

solution.concept: Living and dead cells of plant tissues
solution.explanation: Dead at maturity: tracheids (dead, without protoplasm), vessel members (devoid of protoplasm), sclereids (highly thickened dead cells) and phloem fibres (lose their protoplasm and become dead at maturity). Living: xylem parenchyma, companion cells, sieve tube elements (living, with peripheral cytoplasm, though without a nucleus) and collenchyma. So 4 are dead.
steps: Dead: tracheids, vessels, sclereids, phloem fibres = 4
Living: xylem parenchyma, companion cells, sieve tube elements, collenchyma
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 wrongly counts sieve tube elements as dead because they lack a nucleus. 3 forgets that phloem fibres die at maturity. 6 counts both sieve tube elements and companion cells as dead.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Permanent Tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option B: 4

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Apical meristems and intercalary meristems are called primary meristems.
Reason (R): They appear early in the life of a plant and contribute to the formation of the primary plant body.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT explains that apical and intercalary meristems are primary meristems because they appear early in the life of a plant and contribute to the formation of the primary plant body. Lateral meristems, which appear later, are secondary meristems.
steps: R: true, and it is the reason for the name
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Meristematic Tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (cell or tissue) with List-II (nature of the cell wall).

List-I:
A. Parenchyma
B. Collenchyma
C. Sclerenchyma
D. Endodermis of a dicot root

List-II:
I. Thin walls made of cellulose
II. Thickened at the corners by deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin
III. Thick and lignified walls with a few or numerous pits
IV. Tangential and radial walls with a deposit of suberin as Casparian strips

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Parenchyma cells have thin cell walls made of cellulose. Collenchyma cells are thickened at the corners due to deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin. Sclerenchyma has long, narrow cells with thick and lignified walls with a few or numerous pits. The endodermal cells of the root have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy suberin on their tangential and radial walls in the form of Casparian strips.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap parenchyma and collenchyma, sclerenchyma and endodermis, or collenchyma and sclerenchyma.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues; Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements comparing collenchyma and sclerenchyma are correct?

(a) Both provide mechanical support.
(b) Collenchyma cells may contain chloroplasts, in which case they assimilate food.
(c) Both have lignified cell walls.
(d) The walls of sclerenchyma cells have a few or numerous pits.
(e) Collenchyma cells have large intercellular spaces between them.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Collenchyma provides mechanical support to growing parts such as the young stem and petiole; its cells often contain chloroplasts and then assimilate food; its walls are thickened at the corners with cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin, and intercellular spaces are absent. Sclerenchyma provides mechanical support to organs; its cells have thick, lignified walls with a few or numerous pits.
steps: (e): false, collenchyma has no intercellular spaces
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (c) or (e), or leaves out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Permanent Tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (d) only

In the dicot root this includes the conjunctive tissue (parenchyma between xylem and phloem). The endodermis is the innermost layer of the cortex and lies outside the stele.

Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

The existence of bulliform cells has nothing to do with the shape of the guard cells, so R does not explain A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In the transverse section of a plant organ, the xylem and phloem lie on different radii, the endodermis has Casparian strips, and the pith is large and well developed. Which of the following conclusions are correct?

(a) The section is of a monocot root.
(b) The protoxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ.
(c) Cambium is present between the xylem and the phloem, so the bundles are open.
(d) There are usually more than six xylem bundles.
(e) The xylem and phloem lie together on the same radius.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Xylem and phloem on different radii means radial vascular bundles, found in roots; a Casparian endodermis confirms a root. A large, well-developed pith is a feature of the monocot root, which usually has more than six xylem bundles (polyarch). In roots the primary xylem is exarch, with protoxylem towards the periphery. Radial bundles have no cambium between xylem and phloem in the primary structure, and monocot roots do not undergo secondary growth.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (c) or (e), which contradict the radial arrangement, or leaves out a correct conclusion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (Monocotyledonous Root)

solution.concept: Extent of the ground tissue system
solution.explanation: All tissues except the epidermis and the vascular bundles constitute the ground tissue. In a dicot stem this includes the hypodermis, cortical layers, endodermis, pericycle, medullary rays and pith. Protoxylem and companion cells are parts of the vascular bundles, and the epidermis belongs to the epidermal tissue system.

Hypodermis and medullary rays → ground tissue

(a) Tracheids
(b) Vessel members
(c) Sclerenchyma cells
(d) Collenchyma cells
(e) Companion cells

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Tracheids are elongated, tube-like cells with thick and lignified walls and tapering ends. A vessel member has lignified walls and a large central cavity. solution.explanation: In prokaryotes, ribosomes are about 15 nm by 20 nm in size and are made of two subunits, 50S and 30S, which together form the 70S prokaryotic ribosome. The eukaryotic 80S ribosome has 60S and 40S subunits.
solution.why_others_wrong: 60S and 40S are the subunits of the eukaryotic 80S ribosome. S values are sedimentation coefficients and are not simply added, so pairs chosen to add up to 70 are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells (Ribosomes and Inclusion Bodies)

solution.explanation: The chloroplasts in green plants are lens-shaped, oval, spherical, discoid or even ribbon-like, with a length of 5–10 µm and a width of 2–4 µm. They are double membrane-bound, and the space limited by the inner membrane is called the stroma, in which the thylakoids lie.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: How many individual microtubules are present in the 9 + 2 axoneme of a cilium, and in the nine peripheral fibrils of a centriole, respectively?

solution.explanation: The axoneme has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules and a pair of centrally located microtubules: 9 × 2 + 2 = 20. A centriole has nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin, each of which is a triplet: 9 × 3 = 27.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11 and 9 count fibrils, not individual microtubules. 20 and 18 treats the centriole fibrils as doublets. 18 and 27 forgets the central pair of the axoneme.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A protein synthesised by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum is to be secreted from the cell. Which route does it most likely follow?

options.text: Trans face of the Golgi apparatus → cis face → rough ER → outside the cell
Rough ER → cis face of the Golgi apparatus → trans face of the Golgi apparatus → outside the cell
Smooth ER → lysosome → nucleus → outside the cell
Rough ER → trans face of the Golgi apparatus → cis face → outside the cell

solution.explanation: The Golgi cisternae have a convex cis (forming) face and a concave trans (maturing) face. Materials to be packaged come from the ER, fuse with the cis face and move towards the trans face. Many proteins synthesised by ribosomes on the ER are modified in the Golgi cisternae before they are released from its trans face; the Golgi apparatus packages materials to be secreted outside the cell.
steps: Leaves from trans face for secretion
solution.why_others_wrong: The cis face receives and the trans face releases, so routes that go trans → cis are reversed. Lysosomes and the nucleus are not on the secretory route.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Endomembrane System (Golgi Apparatus)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Rough ER → cis face of the Golgi apparatus → trans face of the Golgi apparatus → outside the cell

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which division reduces the number of chromosomes to half, so that the two cells formed have half the chromosome number of the parent cell?

solution.explanation: In anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids remain together, so each of the two cells formed at the end of meiosis I has half the number of chromosomes of the parent meiocyte. questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Yeast can progress through the cell cycle in about 90 minutes. Starting from a single yeast cell, and assuming every cell completes a cycle and divides into two every 90 minutes, how many cells will be present after 6 hours?

solution.explanation: 6 hours = 360 minutes. Number of cycles = 360 / 90 = 4. Each cycle doubles the number of cells, so the number of cells = 2⁴ = 16.

solution.concept: Why meiosis gives four haploid cells

solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A cell of a diploid plant has 2n chromosomes and 4C DNA. Its chromosomes have not yet condensed, and its nuclear envelope and nucleolus are intact. The cell is most likely in the:

solution.concept: Identifying a phase from DNA content
solution.explanation: DNA doubles from 2C to 4C in the S phase while the chromosome number stays 2n. A cell with 4C DNA whose chromosomes are still uncondensed, with an intact nucleus, has completed S but not begun prophase, so it is in G2, when proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis.
steps: 4C + 2n + intact nucleus → after S, before prophase → G2
solution.why_others_wrong: G1 and G0 cells have 2C DNA. A nucleus at telophase II has n chromosomes and 1C DNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (Phases of Cell Cycle)
solution.final_answer: Option B: G2 phase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about cytokinesis in a plant cell are correct?

(a) The new cell wall begins as a simple precursor called the cell plate.
(b) Wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls.
(c) Cytokinesis takes place by a furrow in the plasma membrane that deepens towards the centre.
(d) Organelles such as mitochondria and plastids get distributed between the two daughter cells.
(e) The cell plate later becomes the secondary wall.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Plant cells are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, so cytokinesis is by cell plate formation, not furrowing. Wall formation starts in the centre and grows outward to meet the lateral walls. The cell plate represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells. At cytokinesis, organelles like mitochondria and plastids are distributed between the daughter cells.
steps: (c): false, furrowing is seen in animal cells
(e): false, the cell plate represents the middle lamella
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (c) or (e), or leaves out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Cytokinesis)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Interkinesis is generally long-lived, and DNA replicates during it.
Statement II: Anaphase I separates homologous chromosomes, while anaphase II separates sister chromatids.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The stage between the two meiotic divisions, interkinesis, is generally short-lived, and there is no replication of DNA during it. In anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate while the sister chromatids stay associated at their centromeres; in anaphase II the centromere of each chromosome splits and the sister chromatids move to opposite poles.
steps: Statement I: false, interkinesis is short and has no DNA replication
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Meiosis I; Meiosis II)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cells in the quiescent stage (G0) remain metabolically active.
Reason (R): Cells in G0 keep proliferating continuously, whatever the requirement of the organism.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Cells that do not divide further exit G1 and enter G0. Cells in this stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so, depending on the requirement of the organism. So A is true and R is false.
steps: R: false, G0 cells do not proliferate unless called on to do so
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (Phases of Cell Cycle)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about a cell at metaphase II of meiosis in a diploid (2n) organism are correct?

(a) The cell has n chromosomes.
(b) Each chromosome has two chromatids.
(c) The homologous chromosomes are paired as bivalents.
(d) Microtubules from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores of the sister chromatids.
(e) The cell has 4C DNA.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes, so each cell entering meiosis II has n chromosomes, each still made of two sister chromatids (2C DNA, half of the 4C of the meiocyte after S phase). At metaphase II the chromosomes align at the equator and microtubules from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids. Bivalents exist only in prophase I and metaphase I.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (c) or (e), or leaves out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Meiosis II)
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the oocytes of some vertebrates, diplotene can last for months or years.
Reason (R): Diakinesis is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements are true. A concerns the duration of diplotene in vertebrate oocytes. R describes the next stage, diakinesis, in which chiasmata terminalise. The terminalisation of chiasmata in a later stage does not explain why diplotene is prolonged, so R is not the explanation of A.
steps: R describes a different stage; it does not explain A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Prophase I)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following takes place in anaphase I of meiosis, but in neither the anaphase of mitosis nor anaphase II of meiosis?

options.text: Separation of homologous chromosomes, while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres
Movement of chromosomes towards the opposite poles
Shortening of the microtubules attached to the kinetochores

solution.explanation: In anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate, while the sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres. In the anaphase of mitosis and in anaphase II the centromeres split and sister chromatids separate. Movement towards the poles occurs in all three anaphases.
steps: Anaphase I: homologues separate, centromeres intact
Mitotic anaphase and anaphase II: centromeres split, chromatids separate
solution.why_others_wrong: Splitting of the centromere occurs in mitotic anaphase and anaphase II, not anaphase I. Poleward movement and the shortening of kinetochore microtubules are not unique to anaphase I.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Anaphase); Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Separation of homologous chromosomes, while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cell growth, in terms of cytoplasmic increase, continues through the cell cycle, but DNA is synthesised in only one specific stage.
Statement II: In animal cells, DNA replication begins in the nucleus during the S phase, while the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Growth and DNA synthesis in the cell cycle
solution.explanation: NCERT states that although cell growth (in terms of cytoplasmic increase) is a continuous process, DNA synthesis occurs only during one specific stage, the S phase. In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (Phases of Cell Cycle)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A graph that shows the rate of photosynthesis at different wavelengths of light is called the:

solution.explanation: A graph of the absorption of light of different wavelengths by a pigment is its absorption spectrum. A graph of the rate of photosynthesis against wavelength is the action spectrum. NCERT superimposes the two to show that most photosynthesis takes place in the blue and red regions, where chlorophyll a absorbs most.
steps: Rate of photosynthesis vs wavelength → action spectrum
solution.why_others_wrong: The absorption spectrum plots light absorbed by a pigment, not the rate of photosynthesis. The Z scheme shows electron carriers on a redox scale. A chromatogram separates pigments.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', What is our Understanding of the Pigments Involved in Photosynthesis?
solution.final_answer: Option C: action spectrum

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following leaf pigments is NOT an accessory pigment?

solution.explanation: Chlorophyll a is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis and forms the reaction centre. Chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids are called accessory pigments: they also absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a.
solution.why_others_wrong: Chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids are the accessory pigments named by NCERT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', What is our Understanding of the Pigments Involved in Photosynthesis?
solution.final_answer: Option D: Chlorophyll a

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the leaves of a plant, large bundle sheath cells with many chloroplasts, thick walls and no intercellular spaces form a wreath around the vascular bundles. Which of the following plants shows this anatomy?

solution.explanation: This is Kranz ('wreath') anatomy, a characteristic of C4 plants such as maize and sorghum. The bundle sheath cells have a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and no intercellular spaces. Tomato and bell pepper are named by NCERT as C3 plants grown in CO₂-enriched greenhouses.
steps: Wreath of bundle sheath cells → Kranz anatomy → C4 plant (maize)
solution.why_others_wrong: Tomato and bell pepper are C3 plants. Chlamydomonas is a unicellular green alga with no leaves or vascular bundles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option A: Maize

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In photosynthesis, green plants use light energy to drive the synthesis of organic compounds.
Statement II: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from the splitting of water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Photosynthesis is a physico-chemical process by which green plants use light energy to drive the synthesis of organic compounds. In the light reaction, water is split into H⁺, [O] and electrons on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane, and the oxygen evolved comes from this splitting of water.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Introduction; The Electron Transport (Splitting of Water)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The light-harvesting complexes (LHC) of Photosystem I and Photosystem II are located in the:

options.text: outer membrane of the chloroplast envelope

solution.explanation: Within the chloroplast, the membrane system (grana and stroma lamellae) is responsible for trapping light energy. The pigments are organised into two discrete light-harvesting complexes within PS I and PS II, located in the thylakoid membranes. The stroma carries out the enzymatic reactions that synthesise sugar.
solution.why_others_wrong: The stroma is the site of the biosynthetic phase. The chloroplast envelope and the mitochondrial membrane do not contain the photosystems.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where does Photosynthesis Take Place?; What is Light Reaction?
solution.final_answer: Option B: thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Oxygen is evolved in non-cyclic photophosphorylation but not in cyclic photophosphorylation.
Reason (R): The water splitting complex is associated with PS II, which does not take part in cyclic photophosphorylation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why cyclic photophosphorylation releases no oxygen
solution.explanation: Water is split by the water splitting complex associated with PS II, and this is the source of the oxygen evolved. In non-cyclic photophosphorylation PS II and PS I work in series, so water is split and O₂ released. In cyclic photophosphorylation only PS I is functional and the electron is circulated within it, so no water is split and no O₂ is evolved. R directly explains A.
steps: R: true; no PS II in the cyclic flow → no water splitting → no O₂
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Splitting of Water; Cyclic and Non-cyclic Photo-phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are listed by NCERT as special features of C4 plants?

(a) A special type of leaf anatomy
(b) Tolerance of higher temperatures
(c) A response to high light intensities
(d) Lack of photorespiration
(e) A lower productivity of biomass than C3 plants

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT states that C4 plants are special: they have a special type of leaf anatomy (Kranz anatomy), they tolerate higher temperatures, they show a response to high light intensities, they lack a process called photorespiration, and they have greater productivity of biomass.
steps: (e): false, C4 plants have greater productivity of biomass
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (e) or leaves out one of the true features.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are consumed in the Calvin cycle?

(a) CO₂
(b) ATP
(c) NADPH
(d) O₂
(e) Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The Calvin cycle fixes CO₂ (carboxylation), uses ATP for phosphorylation and NADPH for reduction (reduction stage), and uses ATP to regenerate RuBP. O₂ is a product of the light reaction, not an input of the Calvin cycle, and PEP is the CO₂ acceptor of the C4 pathway in mesophyll cells.
steps: O₂: product of light reaction; PEP: C4 pathway
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes O₂ or PEP, or leaves out one of the inputs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Calvin Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Photorespiration results in the synthesis of sugars and ATP.
Reason (R): In photorespiration, RuBP combines with O₂ to form one molecule of PGA and one of phosphoglycolate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In the photorespiratory pathway, RuBP binds O₂ instead of CO₂ and forms one molecule of PGA and phosphoglycolate. There is neither synthesis of sugars nor of ATP and NADPH; rather, CO₂ is released with the utilisation of ATP. So A is false and R is true.
steps: A: false, no sugar or ATP is synthesised
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Photorespiration
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (quantity in the Calvin cycle) with List-II (number).

List-I:
A. ATP used for every CO₂ fixed
B. NADPH used for every CO₂ fixed
C. Turns of the cycle needed to make one glucose
D. ATP used to make one glucose

List-II:
I. 18
II. 2
III. 6
IV. 3

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Energy accounting of the Calvin cycle
solution.explanation: For every CO₂ molecule entering the Calvin cycle, 3 molecules of ATP and 2 of NADPH are required. Six turns of the cycle are needed to make one molecule of glucose, so one glucose uses 6 × 3 = 18 ATP and 6 × 2 = 12 NADPH.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap ATP and NADPH per CO₂, swap turns and total ATP, or confuse ATP per CO₂ with the number of turns.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Calvin Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly shows the path of electrons in non-cyclic photophosphorylation?

options.text: H₂O → PS II → electron transport chain (cytochromes) → PS I → NADP⁺
H₂O → PS I → electron transport chain → PS II → NADP⁺
NADP⁺ → PS I → electron transport chain → PS II → H₂O
H₂O → PS II → NADP⁺ → PS I → electron transport chain

solution.explanation: Electrons lost by PS II are replaced by electrons from the splitting of water. Electrons excited in PS II pass through an electron transport system of cytochromes to PS I, not being used up on the way. Electrons excited in PS I are passed through another chain to NADP⁺, reducing it to NADPH + H⁺.
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option begins at PS I, the third runs backwards, and the fourth places NADP⁺ before PS I.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Electron Transport
solution.final_answer: Option A: H₂O → PS II → electron transport chain (cytochromes) → PS I → NADP⁺

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The bundle sheath cells of C4 plants have a large number of chloroplasts.
Reason (R): Within the mesophyll cells, the chloroplasts align themselves along the walls so that they get the optimum quantity of incident light.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Chloroplasts in two kinds of cells
solution.explanation: Both statements are true. A describes the bundle sheath cells of C4 plants (Kranz anatomy). R describes how chloroplasts are positioned within mesophyll cells in response to light. The positioning of chloroplasts in mesophyll cells says nothing about why bundle sheath cells of C4 plants are rich in chloroplasts, so R does not explain A.
steps: R concerns a different cell type and a different feature
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where does Photosynthesis Take Place?; The C4 Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A plant that has been in bright light is suddenly placed in darkness. Which of the following can continue for some time before stopping?

(a) Carboxylation of RuBP by RuBisCO
(b) Splitting of water
(c) Photophosphorylation
(d) Reduction of PGA using NADPH
(e) Regeneration of RuBP

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Dependence of the biosynthetic phase on light
solution.explanation: The biosynthetic (Calvin) reactions do not directly depend on light; they depend on the ATP and NADPH made in the light reaction. So, immediately after light becomes unavailable, carboxylation, reduction and regeneration continue for some time, using the ATP and NADPH already formed, and then stop. Splitting of water and photophosphorylation are parts of the light reaction and stop when light is withdrawn.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes a light reaction step or leaves out one of the Calvin cycle steps.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where are the ATP and NADPH Used?
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A maize plant and a tomato plant are grown side by side on a hot, brightly lit day. Which outcome is expected, and why?

options.text: Tomato shows the higher rate, because C3 plants have a higher temperature optimum than C4 plants
Both show equal rates, because light is never a limiting factor
Maize stops photosynthesis, because high temperature denatures PEP carboxylase in C4 plants
Maize shows the higher rate of photosynthesis, because C4 plants have a higher temperature optimum, respond to high light intensities and lack photorespiration

solution.concept: C3 and C4 plants under heat and strong light
solution.explanation: C4 plants respond to higher temperatures and show a higher rate of photosynthesis, while C3 plants have a much lower temperature optimum. C4 plants also respond to high light intensities and lack photorespiration, which decreases CO₂ fixation in C3 plants.
steps: Maize: C4 → higher temperature optimum, no photorespiration
solution.why_others_wrong: C3 plants have a lower, not higher, temperature optimum. NCERT does not say light is never limiting (it limits shade plants), and C4 plants are tolerant of high temperatures.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway; Factors Affecting Photosynthesis (Temperature)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Maize shows the higher rate of photosynthesis, because C4 plants have a higher temperature optimum, respond to high light intensities and lack photorespiration

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The splitting of water and the reduction of NADP⁺ take place on the same side of the thylakoid membrane.
Statement II: The protons needed to reduce NADP⁺ to NADPH + H⁺ are removed from the stroma.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The splitting of water takes place on the inner (lumen) side of the thylakoid membrane, so its protons accumulate in the lumen. NADP reductase is located on the stroma side, and the protons needed to reduce NADP⁺ are removed from the stroma. The two events are on opposite sides, which helps build the proton gradient.
steps: Statement I: false, water splitting = lumen side, NADP⁺ reduction = stroma side
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Chemiosmotic Hypothesis
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly traces atmospheric CO₂ through the C4 pathway?

options.text: CO₂ + RuBP → PGA in mesophyll cells → OAA → transported to bundle sheath cells → PEP
CO₂ + PEP → OAA in bundle sheath cells → malic acid → transported to mesophyll cells → CO₂ fixed by RuBisCO
CO₂ + PEP → OAA in mesophyll cells → malic or aspartic acid → transported to bundle sheath cells → CO₂ released → fixed by RuBisCO into PGA
CO₂ + PEP → PGA in mesophyll cells → OAA in bundle sheath cells → RuBP

solution.concept: Path of carbon in the C4 pathway
solution.explanation: In the mesophyll cells, PEPcase fixes CO₂ with PEP to form OAA, a C4 acid. OAA is converted to malic or aspartic acid, which is transported to the bundle sheath cells. There the C4 acid is broken down to release CO₂ and a 3-carbon molecule; the CO₂ enters the Calvin cycle, where RuBisCO fixes it with RuBP to form PGA.
steps: Mesophyll: PEP + CO₂ → OAA → malic/aspartic acid
Bundle sheath: decarboxylation → CO₂ → Calvin cycle
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option uses RuBisCO in the mesophyll, which lacks it. The third places PEPcase in the bundle sheath and RuBisCO in the mesophyll. The fourth makes PGA the product of PEP carboxylation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option C: CO₂ + PEP → OAA in mesophyll cells → malic or aspartic acid → transported to bundle sheath cells → CO₂ released → fixed by RuBisCO into PGA

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In ATP synthase (complex V), the part that is an integral membrane protein complex forming the channel through which protons cross the inner mitochondrial membrane is:

solution.explanation: ATP synthase has two major components, F₁ and F₀. The F₁ headpiece is a peripheral membrane protein complex and contains the site for synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. F₀ is an integral membrane protein complex that forms the channel through which protons cross the inner membrane.
steps: F₁: peripheral headpiece, site of ATP synthesis
solution.why_others_wrong: The F₁ headpiece contains the ATP-synthesising site, not the channel. Cytochrome c and ubiquinone are electron carriers, not parts of ATP synthase.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option C: F₀

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following processes is common to aerobic respiration, alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation?

options.text: Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA

solution.concept: Glycolysis as the common first stage
solution.explanation: In all three, glucose is first broken down to pyruvic acid by glycolysis in the cytoplasm. The fate of pyruvic acid then differs: it is reduced to ethanol and CO₂ or to lactic acid in fermentation, or enters the mitochondria for the link reaction, the TCA cycle and the ETS in aerobic respiration.
steps: Link reaction, TCA cycle, ETS → aerobic respiration only
solution.why_others_wrong: The link reaction, the TCA cycle and the ETS occur only in aerobic respiration.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis; Fermentation; Aerobic Respiration
solution.final_answer: Option B: Glycolysis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Anaerobic organisms can obtain energy from glucose without using oxygen.
Reason (R): All living organisms retain the enzymatic machinery to partially oxidise glucose without the help of oxygen.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The breakdown of glucose to pyruvic acid (glycolysis) does not need oxygen, and all living organisms retain the enzymes for it. In anaerobic organisms glycolysis is the only process of respiration, and it releases some energy as ATP. So R explains A.
steps: R: true; this machinery (glycolysis) is what lets them obtain energy
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the electron transport system, electrons from NADH are oxidised by NADH dehydrogenase (complex I) and transferred to ubiquinone. Ubiquinone is located:

solution.explanation: The ETS is present in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Electrons from NADH produced in the matrix are oxidised by complex I and transferred to ubiquinone located within the inner membrane. Ubiquinone also receives reducing equivalents from FADH₂ through complex II.
solution.why_others_wrong: The outer membrane and the cytoplasm do not carry the ETS. The thylakoid lumen belongs to the chloroplast.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option D: within the inner mitochondrial membrane

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (step of glycolysis) with List-II (what happens).

List-I:
A. Glucose → glucose-6-phosphate
B. Glucose-6-phosphate → fructose-6-phosphate
C. PGAL → 1,3-bisphosphoglyceric acid (BPGA)
D. Phosphoenolpyruvate → pyruvic acid

List-II:
I. Synthesis of ATP
II. Oxidation, with formation of NADH + H⁺
III. Isomerisation
IV. Phosphorylation catalysed by hexokinase

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Glucose is phosphorylated to glucose-6-phosphate by hexokinase, which is then isomerised to fructose-6-phosphate. Later, PGAL is oxidised (two redox equivalents are removed and transferred to NAD⁺, forming NADH + H⁺) and combined with inorganic phosphate to form BPGA. ATP is synthesised when BPGA forms PGA and again when PEP is converted to pyruvic acid.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap isomerisation with oxidation, phosphorylation with isomerisation, or the NADH-forming step with the ATP-forming step.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

Assertion (A): CO₂ is released when pyruvic acid is converted to acetyl CoA.
Reason (R): The conversion of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA takes place in the cytoplasm.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

solution.explanation: Pyruvic acid formed in glycolysis enters the mitochondrial matrix, where it undergoes oxidative decarboxylation by pyruvic dehydrogenase: pyruvic acid + CoA + NAD⁺ → acetyl CoA + CO₂ + NADH + H⁺. questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In which of the following conversions is CO₂ released?

(a) Pyruvic acid → acetyl CoA
(b) Formation of α-ketoglutaric acid in the TCA cycle
(c) α-Ketoglutaric acid → succinyl CoA
(d) Succinyl CoA → succinic acid
(e) Pyruvic acid → lactic acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: CO₂ is released in the oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA, and in the two successive decarboxylations of the TCA cycle, which form α-ketoglutaric acid and then succinyl CoA. The conversion of succinyl CoA to succinic acid synthesises GTP, without decarboxylation, and the reduction of pyruvic acid to lactic acid releases no CO₂.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (d) or (e), or leaves out a decarboxylation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Aerobic Respiration; Tricarboxylic Acid Cycle; Fermentation
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only
